reviewer: independent model (Claude Sonnet subagent, read-only, wrote none of this change)
scope: git diff origin/main...p170 (feedback/README.md, worker.mjs, worker.test.mjs); cross-checked client shape in p171 (3c52d667) DiagnosticReport.swift, FeedbackFacts.swift, AppPermissions.swift

findings.text: Validator is correct as a privacy boundary: permissions must be a non-array object with exactly the 5 keys (exact() checks count plus own-key presence) and every value must be a string in the 6-value allowlist (choice() uses strict includes, so 'allowed\n' and non-strings fail). Extra top-level diagnostics keys still rejected; all 21 required fields still mandatory; absent permissions passes (legacy clients).

Key-count check was replaced by a required-fields check plus an unknown-key scan. Logically equivalent to the old count check with permissions as the single optional extra. Slightly harder to read; no defect found.

Client shape matches: permissions is [String:String]? (synthesized Codable omits nil, so no null is sent, which the Worker would reject), keys exactly accessibility/screenRecording/contacts/messagesDatabase/messagesAutomation, values passed through choice() to the same 6-value set; AppPermissionStatus.diagnosticStatus maps only to allowed/off/notRequested/restricted/notConnected/unknown. permissionStage values also within the Worker's allowlist. No mismatch found.

Deployment ordering matters: the Worker must be deployed before a client with #171 ships, otherwise the old Worker's key-count check rejects every diagnostics submission with 400. README says this; make it an explicit release-checklist step for 0.11.1.

Coverage is good: valid store, retry idempotency, key-order-insensitive dedupe, null/array/empty/bool, extra key, wrong type, free text, trailing newline, missing required field with permissions present. Minor gaps (not blocking): no test for a missing permission key with 5 keys total (e.g. one key replaced by another name) and no explicit legacy no-permissions case in this test, though the pre-existing tests cover absent permissions.

notes: No blockers. Server and client agree on shape and vocabulary. Only residual risk is deploy ordering (Worker before client).
